question.problem:
Find the second-degree Taylor polynomial ${P}_{2}(x)$ of $f(x)=\frac{4}{x}$ about $x=2.$

${P}_{2}(x)=$
{{field-1}}$\,-$
{{field-2}}$(x-2)\,+$
{{field-3}}${(x-2)}^{2}$
question.worked_solution:
To find the second-degree Taylor polynomial about $x=2,$ we plug $a=2$ into the general formula to give

$$
{P}_{2}(x)=f(2)+{f}^{′}(2)(x-2)+\frac{1}{2}{f}^{″}(2){(x-2)}^{2}.
$$

So, we need to work out $f(2),$ ${f}^{′}(2),$ and ${f}^{″}(2):$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x) & =\frac{4}{x} & ⟹ &  & f(2) & =2 \\ {f}^{′}(x) & =-\frac{4}{{x}^{2}} & ⟹ &  & {f}^{′}(2) & =-1 \\ {f}^{″}(x) & =\frac{8}{{x}^{3}} & ⟹ &  & {f}^{″}(2) & =1\end{aligned}
$$

We now plug the results for $f(2),$ ${f}^{′}(2),$ and ${f}^{″}(2)$ into our second-degree Taylor polynomial. This gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{P}_{2}(x) & =2+(-1)(x-2)+1\cdot \frac{1}{2}{(x-2)}^{2} \\  & =2-1(x-2)+\frac{1}{2}{(x-2)}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$
